To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Modified-BPDN bounds on reconstruction error are tighter than BPDN bounds; 2) The modified-BPDN bound holds under fewer sufficient conditions than BPDN bound; 3) When the unknown support is small, the modified-BPDN reconstruction error is much smaller than that of the BPDN reconstruction; and 4) Modified-BPDNP can be used to study the behavior of the BPDNP reconstruction error when the unknown support is large.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of reconstruct a signal from a limited (but large) number of linear measurements, when a fraction of its support is unknown.

the following problem: given noisy measurements of a signal x, where the signal is known to be sparse, i.e. it has only a small number of non-zero elements, and the location of a part of the support is known, find an estimate for x that is as close to x as possible.
the problem of reconstruct a sparse signal when the support is not fully known.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
when the unknown part of the support is small (less than 20%), then modified-BPDN is much more efficient than BPDN, in terms of number of measurements required and reconstruction error.
the modified-BPDN algorithm is a good candidate for recursive sparse reconstruction of a time series of compressive measurements, when the support is only partially known.
modified-BPDN is an effective method for noisy compressive sampling with partially known support, when the unknown support is small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new approach for reconstructing sparse signals from limited noisy measurements, when the support of the sparse signal is only partially known.
modified-BPDN provides a computable and tighter bound on the reconstruction error for the case when the support size is small.
modified-BPDN can be used as a practical tool for noisy compressive sampling with partially known support, when the unknown part of the support is small.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when the unknown part of the support is small, modified- BPDN is a good choice.
when the support of a sparse signal is only partially known, the number of measurements required to reconstruct the signal is smaller than when the support is completely unknown.
when a part of the support is known, one can obtain better bounds and better reconstruction performance than when the support is unknown.
